acceptedAs.reason:
Pass of 00-start produced by two errors cancelling, not a correct layout. Raw Blitz 0.3.0-beta.4 places the overflow:hidden (BFC) green box beside zero-width floats 200 px too low (flow y 250; Chrome 155 print: 42 = top of its wrapper), and the Phase A paginator ignored both that flow position and the `position: relative; top: -100px` of the second green box (it stacked the two boxes under the

), which happened to draw the 200x200 square. With flow positions kept (relative offsets are honoured, Chrome-verified in tests/pagination_gaps.rs a_relative_offset_on_the_first_block_is_kept_and_may_overlap) both boxes land on Blitz's y 250. The remaining failure is the Blitz float/BFC placement (follow-up), not pagination.

Old placement: 34 and 134 (stacked, relative offset ignored). New diff region 200x300 at x 8-207, y 50-349. acceptedAs.reason: False pass of 00-start (WPT reference analysis). The test lays two boxes side by side (an absolutely/relatively positioned stripe next to an in-flow one). The Phase A paginator re-stacked every top-level fragment under the previous one (gap = max(0, flow gap)), so BOTH the test (two block fragments) and the reference (a flattened wrapper whose two inline s became two fragments) were drawn the same wrong way, the second box under the first instead of beside it (for the 3-inch stripes the stacked one leaves no ink in the compared page area: old ink = one stripe, half of Chrome's), and compared equal (maxDifference 0). The step places fragments at their flow positions, so the test now matches Chrome's geometry; what still differs from the reference is a vellora display-list heuristic outside this step: merge_adjacent_rects (RECT_MERGE_TOLERANCE_PX = 4) bridges the real 2-4 px gap between the two background rects of the test, while the reference stripes are images.
acceptedAs.evidence: Old: vellora test == reference (maxDifference 0), ink bbox [8,0,410,225] vs Chrome's test ink [8,19,411,145] (bottom 225 vs 145: stacked, not side by side). New: ink bbox [8,14,410,145] (within 5 px of Chrome's); the only differing pixels are one solid 2x96 px rectangle at x 28-29, y 50-145 (192 px = gap width x stripe height), i.e. exactly the gap between the two stripes that merge_adjacent_rects fills. acceptedAs.reason: Old value produced by two errors cancelling, plus one oracle artefact. Descendants of the DANFE's third table overflow its border box by 2 px; the Phase A paginator clamped the resulting negative flow gap to 0 and pushed every later fragment of page 1 down 2 px (1.5 pt). Chrome's continuous flow puts the fourth table at y 232.73, the step at 233.0 (old 235.0): every box after table 3 is 2 px closer to Chrome (layout-diff: old layer P regressed 345 boxes vs the final layer, the new P moves none), and 431 danfe pdf-probe words improve. position-mm.label: DESIGN TARGET
position-mm.why: word/anchor position error vs a reference (REF-W max/p95, REF-R worst anchor, DANFE-L1, LET-1). 0.1 mm (0.28 pt, 0.38 CSS px) is 10x the 0.01 mm the values are reported with and below one CSS px (0.26 mm), the smallest step a px-snapping layout can move; the measurement is deterministic for one build and one reference (CONFIRMED: equal inputs gave equal values in the Phase A repeat run).

geometry-excess-mm.label: DESIGN TARGET
geometry-excess-mm.why: distance OUTSIDE a specification window (BOL-G*, DANFE-B*, DANFE-M1, TXT-A1). Inside the window the spec admits any value, so only the excess is ratcheted; 0.05 mm is about one 600 dpi raster pixel (0.042 mm), the measurement quantum of measure_bars.py / the page ink box.

font-excess-pt.label: SPEC-derived tolerance unit
font-excess-pt.why: font-size excess outside a window; 0.05 pt is the tolerance ACCEPTANCE.md already applies to every font-size criterion (BOL-T*, DANFE-F*).

count.label: DESIGN TARGET
count.why: integer counts from deterministic tools (required strings found, extractor missing/extra tokens, segments/glyphs attributed, decoded symbols): any loss is a real change of the document.

page-delta.label: DESIGN TARGET
page-delta.why: |vellora pages - reference pages|: a page break moving is never noise.

pdf-probe-pt.label: DESIGN TARGET
pdf-probe-pt.why: per-word |dx| / |dy| of vellora's PDF vs Chrome's PDF (pdftotext -bbox, same-page pairs). 1 pt (0.35 mm) is an order of magnitude below the Phase A regressions it must catch (invoice price column +9 pt, notification signature -14 pt) and above glyph-bbox rounding of pdftotext (0.01 pt) and sub-px snapping differences.
